source_name: Wikimedia Commons + Wikipedia image API + Wikidata P18 + Commons category — airport image gallery

license.name: Mixed (per-file licenses preserved on each airport_image_assets row)
license.attribution: Per-file license + author metadata are preserved in airport_image_assets.extmetadata and exposed via the API as licenseShortName / artist / creditLine. Most airport photos on Commons are CC BY-SA; some are public domain. The worker does not insert fake images and only writes one is_hero=true per airport.

what_it_provides: Image candidates for an airport's image gallery: (1) the Wikipedia article's image list (titles), (2) Commons imageinfo (url / thumburl / mime / size / extmetadata), (3) Commons category members for the airport's Commons category, and (4) Wikidata P18 (main image) plus the P373 Commons-category hint. Candidates are normalized, ranked, deduplicated by image_url, and one is selected as the hero image (is_hero=true).

refresh_policy.schedule_note: Worker is invoked by --airport-id / --icao / --batch-test-airports. Default throttle is 1.5s between requests (DEFAULT_SLEEP_SECONDS=1.5) and 2.0s backoff on 429/503. Dry-run by default; --persist required for DB writes.
refresh_policy.current_build_limit: Small batch only — all-airport backfill is intentionally not implemented yet.

freshness_policy.fresh_for_days: not time-bound (images are reference material, not live data)
freshness_policy.notes: Deduplication is by image_url + content_hash; the worker never overwrites an existing image row in a way that loses attribution. Re-runs are safe (deterministic content hash).

raw_storage.bucket: n/a (no raw blob persisted; candidate dicts are normalized in-memory and inserted as airport_image_assets rows)
raw_storage.path_pattern: not applicable — see airport_image_assets table instead

target_tables: airport_image_assets (run-style metadata for image fetches is recorded in airport_image_assets.diagnostics JSONB; there is no separate airport_image_fetch_runs table — see known_limitations)
airport_source_links (image sources are also cross-referenced via source_type='wikimedia_commons' / 'wikipedia' / 'wikidata')

rest: GET /api/airports/:airportId/intelligence (gallery surfaced through the airport intelligence endpoint)
api_endpoints.needs_contract_detail: Whether a dedicated GET /api/airports/:airportId/images endpoint exists; the airport-intelligence route currently serves gallery + profile + modules. Confirm before any frontend work assumes a dedicated images route.

frontend_usage.barrel: apps/web/src/layers/layer_01_aviation/index.ts re-exports useAirportIntelligence and the intelligence types

known_limitations: Dry-run is the default; --persist must be explicit.
Only one is_hero=true per airport (enforced by the unique partial index idx_airport_image_assets_single_hero).
Image candidates are capped at 8 per airport (max_images default) to bound DB writes and request volume.
All-airport backfill is intentionally not implemented yet (see worker docstring: 'Sources NOT used yet — All-airport backfill').
Social media / official airport websites / Flickr / aviation photography sites are explicitly NOT used yet (per worker docstring).
Test airport list is hard-coded: TEST_AIRPORTS = ['KBDL', 'KBOS', 'KPVD', 'KJFK', 'KLAX', 'EGLL', 'OMDB', 'VIDP', 'WSSS', 'RJTT'].
The 429/503 backoff loop is the only documented retry strategy; no general exponential backoff for non-rate-limit errors.

There is no separate airport_image_fetch_runs table; per-fetch diagnostics land in airport_image_assets.diagnostics JSONB (constraint permits, but the worker today does not write a row per fetch attempt — it writes per asset).
pipeline_source_id_note: The image-gallery worker does not write a single bundled source_id; each airport_image_assets row carries a source_type enum ('wikimedia_commons' / 'wikipedia' / 'wikidata' / 'official_site' / 'manual' / 'other') and per-row attribution. This catalog entry groups the Wikimedia-side providers (Commons + Wikipedia image list + Wikidata P18 + Commons category) under a single 'source' for the source-catalog.
notes: This catalog source_id ('wikimedia_commons_airport_images') groups Wikimedia Commons, Wikipedia image lists, and Wikidata P18 under one logical source for catalog purposes. The DB rows record the actual source_type per image.

Worker docstring lists 'Wikimedia Commons: imageinfo for file metadata' and 'Wikimedia Commons category: category members' alongside the Wikipedia image list and Wikidata P18 as the four Wikimedia-side channels. Wikipedia REST and Wikidata are registered separately in the source-catalog for the public-profile pipeline.
